spec.question: Can two independently qualified canonical two-level request/effect controllers compose at execution time into one bounded three-level chain, with L2 requesting L1, L1 independently choosing/requesting L0, and no upward acquisition of L0 local means or generic hierarchy-manager authority?
spec.incumbent: The canonical two-level request/effect/currentness architecture is composable one execution level deeper by treating a qualified middle controller as an opaque subordinate handler; no new hierarchy manager or semantic role identity is needed.
spec.rival: The apparent third level is either a flattened direct L2→L0 fixture in disguise, or nesting requires the top harness to choose the leaf request / import lower-level means, or introduces new cross-level execution authority.
spec.manipulation: Build two independent MS2063 integrated controllers on the same canonical code. Keep the top controller’s learned request/routing state unchanged, but replace its opaque subordinate request handler with a nested handler that maps only the top request token to one middle current raw context. The middle Microseed must then call its own qualified current_proposal, nominate its own bounded intent, and execute its own bound L0 request. Execute one distinct top request from each top learned class. Compare top-level observed consequences with an ordinary flattened MS2063 control.
matched_controls: ordinary flattened MS2063 top controller under the same two query classes
two independent middle classes so no duplicate-proposal reuse
top and middle capability registries inspected for namespace separation
no leaf target passed into top current_proposal or top handler input
no semantic Parent/Child labels used in routing
spec.incumbent_prediction: Each top class selects its own bound L1 request; inside that handler the middle controller independently selects the correct bound L0 request for the requested middle class and executes it; top observation remains HIGHER-GOOD/+2 and matches flattened control; top registry never contains middle bound L0 capability IDs or leaf local means; no hierarchy_manager/parent_manager/desired_state_registry appears.
spec.rival_prediction: The nested case needs the harness/top controller to supply a leaf request, exposes/installs L0 means in the top registry, fails to preserve top consequence, or requires a new manager/authority surface not present in the two-level components.
spec.measurement: Top proposal sequence/target and observed effect; middle proposal sequence/leaf target and local mean; capability-registry separation; action intent/execution counts at each layer; forbidden manager/semantic-authority surfaces; flattened-vs-nested top observable equivalence.
spec.falsifier: Any leaf target is supplied by L2/harness as part of the top request decision, any L0 local mean/capability enters L2’s capability registry, nested execution cannot produce the same top consequence through middle-owned selection, or nesting requires a new cross-level manager/authority object.
assistance_controls: Middle raw context corresponding to the L1 request is harness-supplied operational structure and remains an explicit assistance ceiling.
Both controllers are pre-trained/qualified two-level controllers; this test does not establish three-level end-to-end learning.
authority_controls: L2 sees only its own bound request token and handler receipt; no L0 target or local mean is an L2 execution premise.
Middle proposal/action authority remains ordinary current Microseed authority; no authority is inherited upward from leaf execution.
currentness_restart_controls: Not claimed in this first nested-execution discriminator; cross-level propagation after middle internal drift remains a successor seam.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Research-only test composing two existing MS2063 fixtures; no microseed production changes.
spec.loop_plus: If nesting succeeds, next pressure cross-level currentness/actual-outcome propagation after internal middle drift before any broader recursion claim.
